plotSections.title: Carlkin's study
bullets: The party enters Carlkin's study, leaving Elrus, Araden, and Benji outside in conversation. A day later the floor is still torn up: flagstones upheaved around a sandbox-like wreck in the center of the room.
Carlkin goes to a corner desk and has Walker set the helm on a small altar-like lectern while Carlkin sorts papers. The scene cuts away before any result.

plotSections.title: Finding Haldor
bullets: Gerk looks for Sheriff Haldor alone in the New Navel market. A living vendor, Joanna, directs him south-west: past the tavern, down the road, then right, to Haldor's house.

Gerk pays Joanna one gold for a small wicker chicken and refuses her life-size wicker goose. He says killing geese on sight is religious, calls them evil, and points at the caged-goose vendor two doors down with 'I'll be back for you.'

Haldor is relaxed on his porch in a rocking chair and hat, and he recognizes Gerk after a long absence. He agrees to come help, and he tells Gerk not to threaten villagers. He knows Joanna's chicken and calls the goose-seller a decent vendor whose flock is caged.

plotSections.title: Spirits, the door, and the file
bullets: Gerk says Sylan, his short elven friend with a normal sword that looks big on him, sent him to get Haldor's help rounding up bad spirits and sending them on. He describes spirits flying into Sylan like a jug. Haldor did not know Sylan did this, asks what changed and whether it was looked at, and jokes that he could eat some. Sylan is just outside the gate; they head there so Haldor can hear it from him. None of the party has been taken.

Haldor says Carlkin reported yesterday's doorway: an extradimensional door, which is not allowed inside the city, described as a hell portal in Carlkin's commons. Gerk says his other doors were interdimensional and that he did not know this one would be extradimensional. He claims he fixed the floor; the study is still wrecked, and Carlkin has also reported on it.

Carlkin filed vandalism charges. Haldor has not pursued them: the stronghold is a long walk, and if he waits a day or two the party will be gone and the paperwork goes away. He keeps a file on all of them under the label stronghold hooligans, and most of it is from Carlkin. Gerk says they will apologize and expects Carlkin to yell.

chronologicalEvents: The party enters Carlkin's study; Elrus, Araden, and Benji stay outside and talk. The floor is still a mess one day on, flagstones torn up around a sandbox-like pit.
Carlkin has Walker place the helm on a small altar-like lectern in the corner study and starts through papers. The DM cuts away.
Gerk goes alone to the New Navel market to find the sheriff and asks a living vendor rather than a spirit.
Joanna points him south-west toward Haldor's house: behind the tavern, down the road, then right.
Gerk gives Joanna one gold and takes her wicker chicken. He turns down a life-size wicker goose, says he must kill geese on sight, and threatens the caged-goose vendor two doors down in jest.
Gerk finds Haldor resting on his porch. Haldor remembers him and agrees to help Sylan send bad spirits on after Gerk calls Sylan a spirit jug.
Haldor warns Gerk not to threaten villagers, notes Joanna's chicken, and defends the goose vendor.

On the way to Sylan outside the gate, Haldor says extradimensional doors are banned in the city, that Carlkin reported a hell portal in his commons, and that Carlkin filed vandalism charges. Gerk says he fixed the floor and that his usual doors are interdimensional.
Haldor says the party has a file he labels stronghold hooligans, mostly Carlkin's complaints, and that he may drop it if they leave in a day or two. Gerk promises an apology.

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like person in Langdale; his New Navel lighthouse is home and bookshop.
notes: His study floor is still destroyed a day later: upheaved flagstones around a sandbox-like mess in the center.
He uses a corner desk and a small altar-like lectern, and he starts an examination by having Walker set the helm there while he goes through papers.
He reported Gerk's doorway to Haldor as a hell portal in his commons and also reported on the floor.
He filed vandalism charges against Gerk. Most of Haldor's file on the party comes from him.
Gerk calls him grumpy and expects yelling if they apologize.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter; holds the helm Carlkin agreed to examine.
notes: At Carlkin's direction he sets the helm on the corner lectern. The examination is interrupted before a result.

Helm.existing: A helm Carlkin agreed to examine by appointment.
notes: The appointment is underway: Walker places it on a small altar-like lectern in Carlkin's study while Carlkin sorts papers. No finding is given before the cut.
He searches New Navel alone for Haldor, asks a living market vendor for directions, and goes to Haldor's house.

He buys Joanna's wicker chicken for one gold and refuses a life-size wicker goose. He says killing geese on sight is religious and that they are evil little birds, and he tells Haldor he threatened the goose vendor, mostly in jest.
He tells Haldor that Sylan sent him to get help sending bad spirits home, and that spirits fly into Sylan like a jug. He says Sylan has not taken anyone in the party.
He says he did not know the Carlkin door would be extradimensional, because his other doors were interdimensional. He claims he fixed Carlkin's floor and says they will apologize.
Haldor has not seen him in quite some time and already has him in the stronghold hooligans file.
personality: Treats geese as a religious enemy and will say so to a sheriff.
Sorry about the portal, and sure Carlkin will still yell at him.
quotesThemes: I have to kill geese on sight. That's like a religious thing.
Those are like evil demon little birds.

Joanna.existing: New Navel market vendor who sells wicker animals.
notes: She is a living person in the town market, not a spirit. She directs Gerk south-west to Haldor's house: tavern, down the road, then right.
She sells Gerk a small basket-woven chicken for one gold, then offers a one-to-one wicker goose and says she can make geese or a gander.
Haldor recognizes the chicken as hers and says she makes good geese.

Wicker chicken.existing: A small basket-woven wicker chicken Gerk buys from Joanna for one gold.
notes: Gerk pays the gold and takes it. He is carrying it when he meets Haldor, who recognizes it as Joanna's.

Goose vendor.existing: Caged-goose seller two doors down from Joanna.
notes: He is in the New Navel market with a flock of geese and nothing else, kept in cages. Gerk points at him and says he will be back, and later tells Haldor the threat was mostly in jest.
Haldor calls him a decent vendor, says the cages make the flock harmless, and tells Gerk not to threaten villagers. Haldor starts a remark that this man can be difficult, then defends the shop.

Haldor.existing: Sheriff of New Navel who bans doors and spirit-taking inside the city.
notes: He is at home on the porch, boots on a stump, rocking chair, hat brim down, relaxed. He knows Gerk and has not seen him in quite some time.

He agrees to leave his rest and help Sylan with the bad spirits. He did not know Sylan takes spirits in, asks what changed and whether it was looked at, and jokes that he could eat some. He checks that Sylan has not taken the party.
He restates that extradimensional doors are not allowed in the city and says he does not know the interdimensional kind Gerk describes.

Carlkin's report to him is a hell portal in the commons plus the floor. Carlkin filed vandalism charges; Haldor has not worked the case and may let it die if the party leaves in a day or two, since the stronghold is a long walk.
He keeps files on the whole party under the label stronghold hooligans. He forbids threatening villagers and knows both Joanna and the goose vendor.
personality: Relaxed and dry; willing to help, and glad to avoid paperwork.
Firm about city rules and about not threatening locals.
quotesThemes: Extradimensional doors usually are not permitted within the city limits.
I just label it stronghold hooligans.
I can't have you threatening villagers out here.
openQuestions: He asks what changed so Sylan now takes spirits into himself, and whether anyone has looked at it. Gerk does not answer that before the chunk ends.

Sylan.existing: Half-elf rogue whose sword pulls spirits into a gray field.
notes: Gerk tells Haldor that Sylan tasked him with getting help to round up bad spirits and send them to the afterlife, and that spirits fly into Sylan like a jug.

Haldor remembers him as Gerk's short elven friend with a big sword. Gerk says the sword is normal size and only looks big because Sylan is small. Haldor says Sylan had not been taking spirits before and asks what changed.
He is just outside the town gate. Haldor goes to talk to him there. Gerk says Sylan has not sucked up anyone in the party.
quotesThemes: Spirit jug, Haldor's name for how the bad spirits go into him.
openQuestions: Haldor wants to know what changed and whether the spirit-taking was looked at.

New Navel.existing: A familiar stop with Carlkin's lighthouse; trade caravans leave for the party's tavern in Langdale.
notes: The town center has a small open market of vendors. Haldor's house is south-west of that market: past the tavern, down the road, then right.
Extradimensional doors are not permitted inside the city limits. Haldor keeps a sheriff's file on the party here.

Door.existing: A door that stretches reality between places; Gerk's Doorman doorways.
notes: Haldor treats the Carlkin opening as an extradimensional door, banned in New Navel, and calls it a hell portal in Carlkin's commons.
Gerk says he did not know it would be extradimensional, because every other door he has opened was interdimensional. Haldor says he does not know that kind.

misTranscriptions.notes: Gerk is looking for the sheriff.
Gerk leaves the market for Haldor.
Gerk says silent tasked him with finding Haldor.
Haldor repeats the name of Gerk's elven friend with the sword.
Haldor asks where he is; Gerk says just outside the gate.
Gerk warns Haldor he may have threatened that seller.
Haldor says 'you and I both know Gator can be kind of a' while talking about the caged geese. Unclear if it is the vendor's name.
Haldor stumbling over Gerk's word for his usual doors.

openQuestions: Haldor asks what changed so that Sylan takes spirits into himself, and whether it has been looked at. That is unanswered when the chunk ends; they are only just leaving to meet Sylan.

newTerms.name: stronghold hooligans
notes: Haldor's label for the sheriff's file on the whole party. Most of the complaints in it are from Carlkin.

newTerms.name: spirit jug
notes: Haldor's phrase, taken from Gerk, for Sylan holding bad spirits inside himself so they can be sent home.
